issues.problem: The PDF had no text layer at all (0 words on every page).
issues.cause: It was 'printed to PDF' as images.
issues.fix: Every page goes through OCR with a vision model.

issues.problem: OCR took 90–178 s per page.
issues.cause: 'qwen3-vl:4b' is again a Thinking model; the 4b-instruct model does not fit in 4 GB VRAM; Ollama's default context (4,096) was too small.
issues.fix: Benchmarked on the real page → 'qwen3-vl:2b-instruct' at 1600 px with num_ctx 8192: ~27 s/page, same text.

issues.problem: Page 16: OCR wrote one line 196 times and lost the rest of the page.
issues.cause: Small vision models can get stuck in a repetition loop.
issues.fix: Detect loops (compression ratio / repeated lines) and retry once with repeat_penalty 1.1; otherwise remove repeats and flag the page ⚠️.

issues.problem: File names with underscores (std10_maths_chapter-3) were not recognised.
issues.cause: In regular expressions '_' counts as part of a word, so word boundaries failed.
issues.fix: Normalise _ - . to spaces before matching.

issues.problem: The Devanagari examples in tutor.py became garbage characters.
issues.cause: I edited the file with PowerShell 5.1 Get-Content/Set-Content, which reads ANSI and writes a BOM.
issues.fix: Rewrote the file in UTF-8, scanned all files, added a test, and stopped using those commands for project files.

issues.problem: The tutor added its own analogy and a stray 'not covered' sentence.
issues.cause: Small model not following instructions strictly.
issues.fix: Stricter rules in the prompt and automatic removal of the stray sentence.

issues.problem: 'Review pages' link crashed when the page was opened on its own.
issues.cause: st.page_link needs the multi-page registry from Home.py.
issues.fix: Button + st.switch_page with a specific error fallback; UI test with a real document added.

code.why: Detect a stuck OCR output: normal pages compress to ~44 % of their size, the stuck page to 7 %.

lessons: Benchmark on the owner's real pages before choosing a model.
Never edit UTF-8 files with Windows PowerShell 5.1 text cmdlets.

code.why: The fix for the hidden ion: move each ion so they sit next to each other instead of on top of each other.
code.snippet:
cursor = 0.0
for atoms in Chem.GetMolFrags(with_h):          # one tuple of atom indices per ion
    xs = [conf.GetAtomPosition(i).x for i in atoms]
    shift = cursor - min(xs)
    for i in atoms:
        p = conf.GetAtomPosition(i)
        conf.SetAtomPosition(i, Point3D(p.x + shift, p.y, p.z))
    cursor += (max(xs) - min(xs)) + GAP_ANGSTROM + 0.8

entries.title: 3D Chemistry Lab, browser-tested simulations and the p5.js 2 crash (Blueprint v1.8)
entries.request: Learning should be dynamic: students should see atoms and their valency electrons being donated or shared in reactions in 3D (experiments may stay 2D). Some simulations do not work (screenshot: Electrolysis of Water — 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading option)'). Check all, be robust and precise. Also check the free AI models I found (Gemini, Stable Diffusion/FLUX, Stable Video 3D, GPT-4o images, Leonardo AI) and implement accordingly.
what_i_did: Reproduced the crash in a real browser: built a checker that opens the exact sealed page in a hidden Edge (installed with Windows), so I could finally SEE simulations myself (screenshots) instead of trusting text checks.

Root cause: in p5.js 2, select.option() returns nothing, so the AI's chained createSelect().option(a).option(b) crashed. Fixed in the lab kit (methods made chainable again) — the old lesson works without regenerating.

Looking at screenshots of all 5 simulations showed more faults no check could see: liquid outside the beaker, an upside-down tripod, blue vitriol white before heating, 'Ticks' label, tubes floating above the water.

Lab kit v2: control helpers, hand-drawn apparatus parts and four complete setups (electrolysis, heating, conductivity, neutralisation with indicator colour charts) — each checked by eye in screenshots and corrected (a wire through the liquid, a wire through the bulb).

Simulation pipeline now: safety → lab-kit rules → syntax → run in hidden browser pressing every control → picture review by a vision model (start + DURING/AFTER each control) → problems back to the AI (3 rounds). Remaining picture notes are shown to the teacher.

3D Chemistry Lab: reactions.py computes ionic scenes (electron transfer → ions → attraction), covalent scenes (shared pairs, full shells) and reaction scenes (bonds break, atoms move, charges change, counts equal) from atomic numbers, the reviewed table and balanced equations; chem3d.js (hand-written, no library) draws and animates them. New page, Lesson Studio tab and Teach Mode slides. Molecule table extended to 72 entries, each verified (atoms and charge match the formula).

Evaluated the free models: image generators get electrons/charges/labels wrong and are not interactive; Stable Video 3D needs ~20 GB GPU memory (laptop: 4 GB). Not used for chemistry; possible later for marked illustrations (D33).
Regenerated all 5 simulations; checked each in the checker's pictures. 246 tests pass; README, Blueprint v1.8.

lessons: A check that never RUNS the code cannot find run-time errors — test in the same environment the user sees.

For accuracy, compute science from rules and checked data; use generative AI only where small errors do no harm.

entries.title: History lessons: timeline, map, causes & effects — tested end to end on Class 9 History Ch. 4 (Blueprint v1.9)
entries.request: Build the same kind of teaching app for history, geography, physics and maths chapters; consider free vision models for images/videos. Then: here is a history chapter (Class 9 – History – 4th Chapter, 'Economic Development'); do it accordingly, check end to end before finalising, and record everything in the learning log and other documents.
what_i_did: Explained feasibility first: the existing pipeline is subject-independent; accurate visuals come from checked data + hand-written drawing code; free image/video generators are only for marked decorative pictures (they invent maps, labels and 'photos' of real people). Proposed order: history → geography → physics → maths → narrated videos.

Ingested the chapter (8 pages, text layer, 0 OCR, metadata from the filename) and inspected the text: on two-column pages the PDF order put the right column first and split a 'Do you know?' box mid-sentence. Wrote a column-aware, line-level reader (paragraphs from indents, page numbers dropped) and re-extracted the (not yet reviewed) chapter.

Built history lessons: subject profile, whole-chapter lesson writing, a history prompt (timeline, periods, people, places with a nearby-city hint, causes → effects) and a fact checker (dates with month and event words together in the textbook text; names present; duplicates merged; ranges become periods; exercise passages removed).

Built an offline map of India: Natural Earth India point-of-view boundaries (public domain) + GeoNames India (563 000 places, CC BY 4.0) in assets/geo with SHA-256, a reproducible scripts/build_geo.py, and a place finder that places a name only when the choice is clear.
Reused the textbook's own captioned pictures (4 found: Bhilai Steel Plant, Textile Mill, P. V. Narasimha Rao, Dr Manmohan Singh) for slides and people cards.

Wrote the hand-written history player (timeline with plans as numbered bars and a ≈ break for empty decades, map with non-overlapping labels, causes → event → effects), new Lesson Studio tabs and Teach Mode slides.

Ran the end-to-end test three times on a COPY of the data (so the teacher's own review stays untouched), fixing what each run found; final run: 4 sections (pages 1–7), 11 verified timeline events, 9 plans, 10 people, 3 cause-effect charts, 11 of 16 places placed and none wrong, Studio (6 tabs) and Teach Mode (13 slides) without errors, tutor correct with page references.
270 automated tests pass (24 new); README section 3e, Blueprint v1.9 (D34–D37), code-workflow map updated.

issues.problem: Two-column pages came out in the wrong order (right column first; a box split a sentence).
issues.cause: Plain PDF text follows the file's internal order.
issues.fix: Column-aware reading at line level.
issues.type: Found while inspecting the owner's chapter

issues.problem: My first column reader used text blocks; a test page showed PyMuPDF can merge two columns into one block.
issues.cause: Block-level assumption.
issues.fix: Line-level reader.
issues.type: Claude design gap (caught by a test)

issues.problem: Every line of a 'Do you know?' box became its own paragraph, which split '…14 banks on 19th July 1969' and made the date check reject a true event.
issues.cause: Indentation compared with the column margin instead of the previous line.
issues.fix: Compare with the previous line; the date check ignores line breaks.
issues.type: Claude bug (found by the end-to-end test)

issues.problem: The first lesson used only 3 of 8 pages.
issues.cause: Topic search with a relevance threshold.
issues.fix: A chapter that fits is given whole, in page order.
issues.type: Design gap (found by the end-to-end test)

issues.problem: The AI paired the real year 1991 with an event the textbook gives no year for.
issues.cause: My first check only confirmed the number existed in the page.
issues.fix: Date numbers, month and event words must appear together.
issues.type: Claude check too weak (found by the end-to-end test)

issues.problem: The exercise page (blanks and deliberately wrong pairs) was used as lesson evidence.
issues.cause: No exercise filter; later only its first passage was detected.
issues.fix: Exercise passages removed to the end of their page.
issues.type: Design gap (found by the end-to-end test)

issues.problem: Wrong map places: 'Shivdi' → Shirdi (~200 km away); 'Paral', 'Dadar', 'Damodar' → unrelated villages; 'Visakhapatnam' → Rasapudipalem.
issues.cause: Spelling matches and state-only hints accepted small villages; alternate names beat main names.
issues.fix: Main names first; state hints only for real towns; spelling matches only near a named city or for cities ≥ 100 000; otherwise a reason and a hint box.
issues.type: Claude rules too loose (found by testing)

issues.problem: Map outlines came out empty; old names (Madras, Plassey) missing.
issues.cause: Douglas–Peucker on a closed ring; only 12 alternate names kept.
issues.fix: Split rings before simplifying; keep 40 alternates.

issues.problem: Only 1 of 4 textbook pictures found.
issues.cause: Captions start 1–2 pt inside the picture's edge.
issues.fix: Allow a small overlap.

issues.problem: Timeline unreadable: one 1882 event squeezed 1950–2002 into a third of the width; map labels too small; plan names missing from short bars.
issues.cause: Linear year axis; tall map shrunk to fit; labels only inside bars.
issues.fix: ≈ break for empty decades, bigger map labels, numbered bars with a legend.

issues.problem: During testing a lesson plan was written twice (≈ 2.5 ¢ extra) and the lesson reset to draft.
issues.cause: My test script called the planner directly while the queued planning job was later run by the app's worker on the copy.
issues.fix: Test-procedure lesson only; the app itself runs the job once.

issues.problem: Streamlit warns that components.html and use_container_width are deprecated.
issues.cause: Newer Streamlit API.
issues.fix: use_container_width replaced now; components.html → st.iframe left as an open item for the next Streamlit upgrade (still works in the pinned 1.64.0).
